author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Anthony Volpe marked his return to the New York Yankees with three hits and a grand slam, driving in a career-high five runs in a 10-3 victory over the visiting Colorado Rockies.

Volpe’s slam highlighted a six-run seventh inning that broke the game open. It was his first major-league appearance since George Lombard Jr. replaced him at shortstop in early August. New York recalled Volpe to play second base while Jazz Chisholm Jr. recovers from a strained right thumb.

Luis Garcia Jr. also hit a two-run homer and reached 30 home runs for the first time in his career. The Yankees completed a three-game sweep and won for the eighth time in 11 games, while Colorado absorbed its 10th loss in 13.

The result moved New York within three games of the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East and opened a 4½-game lead over Boston for the league’s top wild-card position. Volpe’s immediate production gives the Yankees another lineup option as they manage Chisholm’s absence and pursue both the division and postseason seeding.
dek: Volpe drove in a career-high five runs in his first game back with New York, powering a six-run seventh inning in a 10-3 win.
headline: Anthony Volpe returns with grand slam as Yankees sweep Rockies
